text: Cloud Deployment Guide DocuMind AI Cloud Deployment Guide AWS Deployment The AWS deployment topology runs the API on Amazon EKS behind an Application Load Balancer. Raw documents and ingestion manifests are stored in a versioned, encrypted S3 bucket. Managed model access goes through Amazon Bedrock, which hosts both the embedding model and the chat model behind a single IAM-scoped API.

at model behind a single IAM-scoped API. The workload's IAM role is scoped to least privilege: S3 read and write on the project prefix only, and Bedrock InvokeModel only. Logs and metrics flow to CloudWatch. Terraform provisions the S3 bucket, the ECR repository for container images, the IAM role, and the CloudWatch log group. Azure Deployment

Documents are stored in Azure Blob Storage, and managed model access goes through Azure OpenAI Service. Azure Monitor replaces CloudWatch for logs and metrics. Azure Container Registry replaces ECR for image storage. GCP Deployment

es ECR for image storage. GCP Deployment The GCP equivalent runs the API on Google Kubernetes Engine. Documents are stored in Google Cloud Storage, and managed model access goes through Vertex AI. Cloud Monitoring replaces CloudWatch, and Artifact Registry replaces ECR. Scaling and Cost Controls

Scaling and Cost Controls In all three clouds, the API pods are stateless and scale horizontally behind a horizontal pod autoscaler targeting seventy percent CPU utilization, with a minimum of two replicas and a maximum of six. The agent orchestrator enforces a hard maximum step count per run to prevent runaway tool-call loops from driving up managed-model spend.
ops from driving up managed-model spend. Embedding calls are batched wherever possible to reduce per-call overhead. Rollback Procedure

ce per-call overhead. Rollback Procedure If a release causes elevated error rates, the on-call engineer runs a Kubernetes rollout undo to revert to the previous container image, which is retained as one of the last five ReplicaSets. If the problem originates from a bad ingestion rather than bad code, the fix is to restore the previous manifest snapshot from S3 versioning and re-run ingestion only on the affected source paths.

DocuMind AI Platform Overview DocuMind AI is an internal Generative AI platform that turns scattered company documents into a governed, queryable knowledge base. The platform ingests PDFs, HTML pages, plain text files, and exported support tickets, then makes their content available through a hybrid retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) API and an agentic research assistant.

) API and an agentic research assistant. The ingestion pipeline follows a classic ETL pattern. The extract stage reads raw files and pulls out text and metadata regardless of source format. The transform stage cleans the text, collapses whitespace, strips control characters, and applies a PII-scrubbing hook that redacts emails and phone numbers before anything is stored.

phone numbers before anything is stored. The load stage writes the normalized document to a processed store and appends an entry to an audit manifest that records the document id, a content checksum, and the number of chunks produced. Because the manifest is keyed on checksum, re-ingesting an unchanged document is skipped automatically, which keeps the pipeline idempotent.

ly, which keeps the pipeline idempotent. After loading, each document is split into retrieval-sized chunks. Three chunking strategies are supported: fixed-size windows with overlap, a recursive splitter that respects paragraph and sentence boundaries, and a semantic splitter that groups sentences until an embedding-similarity breakpoint is crossed.

edding-similarity breakpoint is crossed. The recursive strategy is the default because it balances chunk coherence with predictable size. Each chunk is embedded into a vector and stored in a vector database alongside its source metadata. The platform also builds a lexical BM25 index over the same chunks.

lexical BM25 index over the same chunks. When a user asks a question, the hybrid retriever queries both indexes and fuses the two score lists using a weighted formula: fused_score equals alpha times the dense similarity score plus one minus alpha times the normalized BM25 score.

s alpha times the normalized BM25 score. The default alpha is 0.6, meaning retrieval leans semantic but still benefits from exact keyword matches, which matters a lot for questions that mention specific error codes, product names, or ticket numbers that a purely semantic model might blur together.

rely semantic model might blur together. The retrieved chunks are assembled into a grounded prompt and passed to a language model, which is expected to answer only from the provided context and to avoid asserting anything the context does not support. Every answer returned by the API includes the chunk ids it was grounded in, so any claim can be traced back to its source document.

n be traced back to its source document. For more complex questions that require multiple lookups, the platform exposes an agent orchestrator. The agent plans a sequence of steps, calls tools such as the retrieval tool or a calculator tool, observes the results, and only produces a final answer once it has gathered enough evidence or hit its step budget.
enough evidence or hit its step budget. The step budget exists specifically to bound cost and latency, since an ungoverned agent loop can otherwise make an unbounded number of expensive model calls.

bounded number of expensive model calls. The platform is designed to run on any of the three major cloud providers. Object storage and managed model access are both hidden behind a provider-agnostic interface, so swapping from AWS S3 and Bedrock to Azure Blob Storage and Azure OpenAI, or to Google Cloud Storage and Vertex AI, is a configuration change rather than a code change.
Incident Response FAQ

Incident Response FAQ Q: The /health endpoint is returning a 503. What should I check first?
A: A 503 from /health usually means the vector store is unreachable. Check the API pod logs for a connection error, then verify the VECTOR_STORE environment variable and, if using Chroma, confirm the persistent volume is mounted correctly. If using the default numpy backend, confirm the data directory is writable.

confirm the data directory is writable. Q: Query latency has spiked above the three second P95 target. What's the likely cause? A: The two most common causes are a cold-started embedding model on a freshly scaled pod, or the upstream managed LLM provider throttling requests.

anaged LLM provider throttling requests. Check the request_latency_seconds histogram on the /metrics endpoint to confirm which stage is slow, and check the cloud provider's status page for throttling incidents. Q: The retrieval_hit_rate metric is trending downward over several days. What does that mean and what should I do?

hat does that mean and what should I do? A: A declining hit-rate gauge usually indicates corpus drift: new documents have been added whose topics aren't well represented by the current embedding model or chunking configuration, or the index has gone stale relative to source changes.

s gone stale relative to source changes. Re-run the offline evaluation harness against a representative query set, compare against the last recorded baseline, and consider re-ingesting or re-tuning the embedding adapter if the regression is confirmed.

adapter if the regression is confirmed. Q: The agent keeps hitting its max_steps limit without finishing. What's going on?
A: This typically means the goal is too complex for the available tool set, or a recent change to the planning prompt regressed step efficiency. Inspect the steps array returned in the agent response to see exactly which sub-queries were issued and where the loop stalled.

were issued and where the loop stalled. Q: All requests are returning 401 Unauthorized. What should I check?
A: Confirm the X-API-Key header is being sent and matches the value mounted into the pod via the Kubernetes Secret. A common cause is a Secret that wasn't updated after an API key rotation.

asn't updated after an API key rotation. Q: The nightly CI build is failing at the image push step. What's the likely cause?
A: Registry credentials for the container registry (ECR, ACR, or Artifact Registry depending on cloud) have most likely expired and need to be rotated in the CI environment's secret store.

New GenAI Developer Onboarding Guide Welcome to the DocuMind AI team. This guide covers what a new GenAI Developer needs to know in the first two weeks. Environment setup: clone the repository, create a Python 3.11 virtual environment, and install dependencies from requirements.txt.

tall dependencies from requirements.txt. Copy .env.example to .env and fill in cloud credentials only if you plan to test against a real cloud provider; the default local configuration runs entirely offline using the dependency-free hashing embedding provider, the numpy vector store, and the stub LLM provider, so you can be productive on day one without waiting on credential provisioning.

hout waiting on credential provisioning. Codebase orientation: the src/etl package handles extraction, transformation, and loading of source documents. The src/genai package contains the core generative AI logic: chunking, embeddings, vector store, hybrid retrieval, the RAG chain, the agent orchestrator and its tools, and the fine-tuning experiment code.

ls, and the fine-tuning experiment code. The src/api package exposes everything as a FastAPI service. The src/cloud package contains the provider-agnostic cloud storage interface and its AWS, Azure, and GCP implementations. The src/monitoring package contains structured logging and Prometheus metrics.

ructured logging and Prometheus metrics. Running things locally: run scripts/run_pipeline_demo.py to ingest the sample documents and print a summary report, then start the API with uvicorn src.api.main:app --reload. The interactive API docs are available at /docs once the server is running.

ble at /docs once the server is running. Testing: run pytest from the repository root to execute the full unit and integration suite. The evaluation harness under tests/evaluation compares dense-only, lexical-only, and hybrid retrieval quality and writes a report used in the RAG evaluation document.

ort used in the RAG evaluation document. Who to ask: the Solution Architect owns the architecture design document and can advise on component boundaries. The MLOps Engineer owns the Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, and CI/CD configuration under infra/. The QA Engineer owns the test plan and can help you write new test cases that follow the existing Given/When/Then format.

Vector store connection timeout after deploy
After the 2.3.0 release, the API pods intermittently returned 503 from /health. Root cause was the Chroma persistent volume claim not being ready before the pod started serving traffic. Added a readiness probe delay and an init container that waits for the volume mount before the main container starts.

mount before the main container starts. Retrieval_hit_rate metric returned to baseline within ten minutes of the fix. Hybrid retrieval alpha tuning request
Sales engineering reported that questions containing exact product SKUs were returning irrelevant answers under the default hybrid alpha of 0.6.

s under the default hybrid alpha of 0.6. Ran the evaluation harness with alpha swept from 0.0 to 1.0 in increments of 0.1 on a labeled query set containing SKU-heavy questions. Confirmed alpha=0.4 improved hit-rate at k=5 for that query subset without regressing the general query set, and exposed alpha as a per-request override in the /query API so callers can tune it per use case.

API so callers can tune it per use case. Agent loop exceeded max_steps on a comparison question
A user asked the agent to compare two configuration options and it hit the six-step cap without producing a final answer. Traced the issue to the planner splitting the goal into four sub-queries plus a calculation step, leaving no budget for the finish step.
, leaving no budget for the finish step. Increased default max_steps to eight for agent runs and added a check that always reserves the final step for synthesis.

During a QA review, a phone number written as [REDACTED_PHONE] with periods instead of dashes was not redacted by the transform stage's PII scrub hook.
Updated the phone number regex in transform.py to also match period-separated formats and added a regression unit test covering dash, period, and parenthesis phone formats.
